title: Erase Two, Write One
statement: The numbers $1, 2, \dots, 10$ are written on a board. Repeatedly, you erase two numbers $a$ and $b$ and write $a + b + ab$. After $9$ steps one number remains. What is it?
insight: a + b + ab = (a+1)(b+1) − 1, so the product of (x+1) over the board never changes.
redHerring: Trying different erase orders to see whether the result changes.
hints: Try to factor $a + b + ab$ by adding 1.
What quantity over the whole board stays fixed?
solution: Since $a+b+ab+1 = (a+1)(b+1)$, the product $\prod(x+1)$ over the board is invariant. Initially it is $2\cdot3\cdots11 = 11!$. At the end it is $x+1$, so $x = 11! - 1 = 39{,}916{,}799$.
